bindings.domain: Coherent registered prefixes transferred into raw MaybeUninit block owners. Explicit destruction callback ends exactly one original-slot lifetime even on unwind; native logical size remains original through the pass; release follows all successful destructors. Original receiver address, descriptor contents and reentrant owner aliases are excluded.

baseline_mismatch.observation: Native Clear with a throwing first destructor stops after D1. Ordinary AllocVec-backed Rust clear continues to D2 through its slice cleanup guard. Historical regression records [1,2] versus native [1].
baseline_mismatch.red_scope: The ordinary safe clear method retains its existing Rust unwind policy. The final passing target validates a separate explicit raw-state protocol; the historical failing test source is archived rather than misrepresented as a fixed safe-clear implementation.

storage_invariants: Admission checks every initialized prefix before callback or ownership transformation; domain rejection returns the original array plus Failure. Empty positive/zero storage is accepted; zero stride only admits coherent empty or retained first-slot state.

Every payload allocation is transferred with into_raw_parts_with_alloc into AllocVec<MaybeUninit<T>,BaseAllocator> using the identical pointer, capacity, layout and allocator. Raw owners are ManuallyDrop. No ordinary initialized T container holds dead slots. The descriptor backbone holds only empty typed vectors and used0.

The raw-state logical used field remains original until every destructor and requested release completes. The ended prefix advances immediately before callback invocation; the contract guarantees that slot lifetime ends even on unwind. The repaired prefix advances only after a complete constructor result has been written into the dead slot.

Live_value tests index bounds and the exact repaired/ended predicate, then forms one reference from the corresponding proven initialized raw slot. No whole initialized slice or ordinary array is exposed during interruption.

Try_into_array returns the state while holes remain. Only complete repair reconstructs original initialized typed lengths; completed Clear reconstructs length0. Each allocation and its original allocator transfer exactly once. Descriptor allocation/capacity are retained but descriptor contents contain placeholders during the protocol.

Dropping a raw state deliberately retains/leaks its payload allocations. It invokes no payload destructors and never dereferences dead slots. This containment fallback is a Rust safety boundary, not a native destructor-equivalence claim. A private test captures raw allocation ownership, drops an interrupted state, repairs the one hole, and reclaims every payload exactly once under strict Miri.
behavior: Twenty-six pinned UBSan rows cover both Clear release modes, success and destructor failure at positions1,2,3,5 across three blocks. Every callback observes original logical size5, three live payload allocations, and its original slot address. On failure no allocation is freed and later live elements remain accessible through the checked raw-state view.

Explicit repair occurs only after failure size/ended/live-tail observations. A subsequent Clear reproduces ascending destruction order with all payload blocks still allocated until the destruction pass finishes. Per-block release then reaches zero outstanding allocation requests.

Catch_unwind tests establish that the original typed destructor panic payload propagates unchanged. Repair can itself panic after a completed earlier repair; both captured payloads remain intact and the exact remaining hole interval survives. Extraction remains rejected until repair completes.

Empty and bounded zero-stride states invoke no destruction callbacks. Zero-stride Clear preserves the pinned destructor omission and permits explicit stride reset after recovering an empty array. Noncanonical initialized tails return the unchanged original array before any transformation.

No Clone, Copy or Default bound is added to the raw state or callback protocol. The native-trace payload implements none of those traits. Original52 tests remain unchanged and join native, normal Rust and strict Miri logs.
limitations: This is a two-phase consuming ownership protocol. Original receiver addresses, cached iterator original-owner identity and reentrant observations through the old receiver are unsupported. The callback receives the raw-state logical-size reference, not permission to alias the original receiver.

The original descriptor allocation/capacity survive, but its entries are empty placeholders during raw ownership. Separate raw-block metadata does not establish native descriptor-content or protected blockAddress reentrant-observer parity.

Unsafe callbacks must end exactly one supplied lifetime even on unwind, retain no slot/metadata reference and neither free storage nor create conflicting aliases. Allocator release must not unwind. The callback contract is not inferred from arbitrary C++ type traits.

Ordinary safe DynamicArray::clear and implicit Drop retain their existing Rust cleanup policy. This receipt does not claim native throwing-destructor parity for that convenience API, implicit destructor unwinding, or other upstream callers until they opt into the explicit protocol.

Containment Drop leaks payload allocations, including never-started raw states. Explicit repair or successful Clear is required for automatic resource reclamation. Repair is caller-selected Rust recovery; native does not automatically reconstruct ended objects.

Later zero-stride sparse slots, unregistered raw lifetimes, incompatible allocation ownership, arbitrary callback reentrancy and release-time allocator exceptions remain outside this bounded domain. Zero-stride omission may deliberately abandon live resource cleanup, as documented by the retained-zero receipt.
The native fixture links pinned prebuilt x86_64 TKernel with UBSan instrumentation in the probe. Historical receipts remain untouched; no shared parity-ledger or global completion claim is added.
validation_scope: Bounded explicit raw-state protocol for Clear(bool) destructor interruption and recovery, with genuine payload addresses and allocator ownership; not full DynamicArray completion.
